bookTitle: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.topic: Forward Contracts (Bilateral Trade) -> Futures Contracts & Daily Marking to Market
facts.statement: Limitation of Forward Contracts (Bilateral Trade): Counterparty credit risk and total lack of liquidity (illiquid bilateral deadlock). (1848 Midwest grain harvest default: Bumper harvest collapsed spot price; buyers defaulted on bilateral promises, leaving farmers bankrupted.). Solution: Futures Contracts & Daily Marking to Market via Daily cash settlement, initial & maintenance margin tiers, and exchange novation eliminating bilateral credit default risk..

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.topic: Futures Contracts & Minimum Variance Hedging -> Determination of Forward & Futures Prices
facts.statement: Limitation of Futures Contracts & Minimum Variance Hedging: Basis risk, tail correlation breakdown, and liquidity strain from cash margin calls during extreme moves. (1993 Metallgesellschaft collapse: Short-term futures roll strategy suffered massive immediate cash margin calls during crude oil backwardation inversion.). Solution: Determination of Forward & Futures Prices via Arbitrage-free pricing F0 = S0 * exp(r*T) and forward-rate duration matching..

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.topic: Futures & Forward Linear Payoffs -> Options Mechanics & Trading Strategies
facts.statement: Limitation of Futures & Forward Linear Payoffs: Symmetrical downside risk: If prices move favorably, futures completely eliminate upside gains while forcing severe margin payments. (Airline hedging fuel at $100/barrel with futures: Oil crashes to $40; airline is locked into paying $100 while unhedged competitors thrive.). Solution: Options Mechanics & Trading Strategies via Upfront premium purchase granting the right without obligation, capping maximum loss strictly to premium paid..

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.topic: Binomial Trees & Intuitive Expected Payoff Pricing -> The Black-Scholes-Merton Pricing Model
facts.statement: Limitation of Binomial Trees & Intuitive Expected Payoff Pricing: Requires estimating the real-world expected drift rate (mu) of the stock, which is statistically impossible to predict accurately. (Option writers underpricing long-term calls by relying on subjective bullish projections, leading to sudden insolvency.). Solution: The Black-Scholes-Merton Pricing Model via Constructing a continuously riskless hedged portfolio (dPi = 0) eliminates the subjective drift rate mu, replacing it with risk-free rate r..

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.topic: Static Black-Scholes-Merton Valuation -> The Greeks & Dynamic Hedging
facts.statement: Limitation of Static Black-Scholes-Merton Valuation: Option risk is dynamic and multi-dimensional: Spot moves, time decays, and volatility changes continuously. (Long option holder being directionally right on stock move but losing 80% of value due to rapid theta decay and implied volatility collapse after earnings.). Solution: The Greeks & Dynamic Hedging via Continuous Taylor-series risk decomposition enabling gamma-neutral and vega-neutral immune portfolios..

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.topic: Lognormal Stock Return & Constant Volatility Assumption -> Volatility Smiles, Skew & Non-Linear Exotics
facts.statement: Limitation of Lognormal Stock Return & Constant Volatility Assumption: Real market return distributions exhibit severe negative skewness, fat tails (leptokurtosis), and crash risk. (Black Monday (October 19, 1987): Out-of-the-money puts experienced 20-standard-deviation moves, bankrupting portfolio insurance funds.). Solution: Volatility Smiles, Skew & Non-Linear Exotics via Implied volatility mapping across strikes and maturities reflecting market crashophobia and jump-diffusion realities..

facts.topic: The Law of Inevitable Counterparty Risk
facts.statement: Bilateral agreements fail without central clearing and daily margin mechanics. Directive: Never enter uncollateralized long-horizon forward commitments without daily variation margin.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.statement: Futures price is determined by financing cost and storage, never subjective future price speculation. Directive: Always price forward commitments using F0 = S0 * exp(r*T) to capture cash-and-carry mispricings.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.statement: Linear tools (futures/swaps) lock in price but forfeit all favorable upside. Directive: Employ options when operational survival requires upside participation or catastrophic floor protection.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.statement: Derivative value depends on continuous dynamic replication, completely independent of expected stock return. Directive: Value all contingent claims in the risk-neutral measure using the risk-free rate r and implied volatility sigma.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.statement: Directional correctness is meaningless if theta decay and vega collapse outpace delta gains. Directive: Monitor delta, gamma, and vega simultaneously; never run naked negative gamma into high-volatility events.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.statement: Constant volatility is a mathematical fiction; tail risk and crashophobia command persistent implied volatility premia. Directive: Price out-of-the-money puts using the empirical volatility surface, never a single flat at-the-money volatility.
